---
title: "2. Labs and baseline data"
format: html

This script reads the CD4 and viral load results and the patient-level information: demographics, insurance, prior care and psychiatry visits. It produces `cd4`, `viral_load` and `baseline` for [3. One row per patient-day](03_person_days.qmd) and [6. Cohort](06_cohort.qmd).

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/02_labs_and_baseline.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/02_labs_and_baseline.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/functions.R)

Translated from Stata Steps [2 (CD4)](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/stata/Do%20Step%202%20CD4.do), [3 (VL)](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/stata/Do%20Step%203%20VL.do), [4 (demographics)](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/stata/Do%20Step%204%20Demographic.do), [4B (insurance)](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/stata/Do%20Step%204B%20Insurance.do) and [4C (psychiatry)](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/stata/Do%20Step%204C%20Psych.do), and the merges at the top of [Step 5](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/stata/Do%20Step%205%20Merge%20and%20Expand.do).

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered. The code has been run only on synthetic data; nothing on this page is a study result.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/02_labs_and_baseline.R")
source("_stata_links.R")
```

## CD4 counts

Each Stata lab step read the file, converted the date, then reshaped to one row per patient with columns `CD4Result1`, `CD4Date1`, `CD4Result2` ... so that it could be merged one-to-one later. R keeps one row per test (long format) and joins by patient and date when needed, so no reshape is required.

```{r}
#| label: read-cd4
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| output: asis
stata_for("read-cd4")
```

## Demographics

Lower-case codes (`f`, `m`, `b`, `h`) are corrected, then indicators are made for the propensity model. Injection drug use and MSM each include the combined `MSM&IDU` category.

A blank ethnicity needs care. In Stata, `generate Black=(ethnicity=="B")` compares the blank text with "B" and gets 0, so the patient counts as not Black and keeps a propensity score. R reads a blank as missing, and `ethnicity == "B"` would give a missing value, which would drop the patient from the weighted analyses. `ethnicity %in% "B"` gives `FALSE` for a missing value, which matches Stata. In Stata, `encode` then turned the text into numbered categories "to save space", which R does not need.

```{r}
#| label: read-demographics
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| output: asis
stata_for("read-demographics")
```

## Combine

Stata's `merge 1:1` keeps patients found in either file and records which in `_merge`; the Step 5 code listed the unmatched patients and then kept them all. `full_join()` does the same. A patient in the lab files but not in the demographics file is kept, with missing demographics.

`merge 1:1` also stops if a patient appears twice in either file. [`check_unique_patients()`](functions.qmd#checking-one-row-per-patient) does that check first, and `relationship = "one-to-one"` makes each join stop rather than duplicate a patient.

```{r}
#| label: combine-baseline
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| output: asis
stata_for("combine-baseline")
```
